name: Shellter AV Evasion (PE Injection)
description: Shellter is a dynamic PE infector that injects shellcode into a legitimate Windows 32-bit executable, making it appear as a normal program while executing a payload. Used in OSCP to bypass AV when delivering msfvenom payloads.
notes: Run shellter on Kali (via wine) or on a Windows host. Requires a legitimate 32-bit PE (e.g., WinRAR installer, putty.exe). In Auto mode, shellter auto-selects injection points. Always use a real-world PE from the target OS architecture. 32-bit only — 64-bit PEs not supported. Stealth mode attempts to keep the original PE functionality intact post-payload. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 14 (Antivirus Evasion).

defense.why_it_works: Shellter is a dynamic PE infection tool that injects shellcode into existing legitimate PE binaries (e.g., PuTTY.exe, WinRAR.exe). Rather than creating a new malicious executable, it identifies execution paths in the legitimate binary, inserts junk code, and injects the payload at a natural execution point. The resulting binary still functions normally — making it appear legitimate in behavior analysis — while executing the payload in a separate thread. The original binary's code flow is preserved, making static analysis harder.
defense.prerequisites: Shellter (Windows tool, runs under Wine on Linux). A legitimate PE binary to infect. Shellcode payload (Meterpreter, custom). Wine on Kali or Windows host for Shellter execution. 32-bit PE target (Shellter 7.x supports 64-bit via paid version).
defense.impact: T1055 Process Injection + T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information. Produces a legitimate-appearing executable that evades signature AV. The infected binary still functions — users are less suspicious. Payload injected via polymorphic code avoids static shellcode signatures.
defense.detection:
Digital signature validation: if the original PE was signed, Shellter injection breaks the signature — WDAC or Authenticode check catches this. Behavioral EDR: PuTTY.exe making outbound C2 connection or spawning cmd.exe is anomalous. Memory scan: injected shellcode in the PE's process memory. AMSI: PowerShell payload within injected code. File hash: original binary hash no longer matches known-good hash.
Process injection by correlating memory manipulation API calls (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory), suspicious thread creation (CreateRemoteThread), and unusual DLL loads within another process's context (DET0508/AN1399).
ptrace- or memfd-based injection through audit logs capturing system calls (ptrace, mmap) targeting running processes along with suspicious file descriptors or memory writes (AN1400).
Memory-based injection via task_for_pid, mach_vm_write, and dylib injection patterns through DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES or manual memory mapping on macOS (AN1401).
defense.artifacts: EDR: signed binary with broken/missing signature executing | Behavior: legitimate tool (PuTTY.exe) making unexpected network connections | WDAC: signature validation failure | Memory: injected shellcode in process space | File hash mismatch vs known-good
defense.prevention:
WDAC with publisher rules: injection breaks the digital signature → binary fails publisher/hash check → blocked before execution. Behavioral monitoring: flag applications making unexpected network connections. SmartScreen: reputation-based blocking for modified known binaries. EDR memory scanning. File integrity monitoring on delivered executables.
Behavior Prevention on Endpoint: Configure endpoint security solutions to block process injection based on common injection sequences; Windows 10 ASR rules can prevent Office applications from code injection.
Privileged Account Management: Use Yama (ptrace_scope) on Linux to restrict ptrace to privileged users; deploy security kernel modules.
defense.evasion: Inject into a less commonly used legitimate binary that the target is expected to run. Use staged payload (small stager that fetches actual payload) — injected code doesn't contain recognizable payload patterns. Test against target AV before delivery. Use 64-bit PE (newer Shellter).
defense.misconfiguration: WDAC not deployed — unsigned/modified executables run freely. SmartScreen disabled. No behavioral monitoring for application network behavior anomalies. No file hash validation on delivered executables.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# WDAC not configured:
# Any PE (including shellter-infected) runs without signature check

# SmartScreen disabled:
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System').EnableSmartScreen  # 0 or absent

# No file hash validation:
# Delivery mechanism (email, file share) doesn't compare against known-good hashes
# → shellter-infected PuTTY.exe indistinguishable from real one to users
defense.secure_config:
# WDAC publisher rules catch signature breakage:
# If PuTTY.exe was signed by Simon Tatham and Shellter breaks the signature:
# WDAC enforced policy: binary fails publisher check → blocked
New-CIPolicy -Level Publisher -FilePath C:\Policy\BasePolicy.xml -UserPEs
ConvertFrom-CIPolicy C:\Policy\BasePolicy.xml C:\Windows\System32\CodeIntegrity\SIPolicy.p7b

# Enable SmartScreen:
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System' -Name EnableSmartScreen -Value 1
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System' -Name ShellSmartScreenLevel -Value Block

# Behavioral: Defender for Endpoint network protection:
Set-MpPreference -EnableNetworkProtection Enabled
# Alert: putty.exe connecting to non-SSH port = anomaly
